chunks: Muḥammad ibn Muslim asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who greets the people during salat (prayer).
He said: “If a Muslim greets you while you are in salat (prayer), then return the greeting to him; you say, ‘Al-salāmu ʿalayka,’ and gesture with your finger.”

key_terms.السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ: the verbal form of greeting to be said in response
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual act of worship during which the ruling applies
key_terms.بِإِصْبَعِكَ: with your finger, indicating a gesture during prayer
key_terms.مُسْلِمٌ: a Muslim, the one initiating the greeting
key_terms.يُسَلِّمُ: offers salām; gives the greeting of peace

ai.seo_question: How should someone respond to salām while in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding returning a greeting while one is in salat (prayer). Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام instructs that if a Muslim greets a person during prayer, he should respond briefly with the greeting and indicate with his finger.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1063 - Muhammad ibn Muslim asked Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) about a person who greets others while in prayer.
Imam (as) said: "If a Muslim greets you while you are in prayer, respond to him by saying, ‘As-salamu ‘alayka,' and gesture with your finger."
